findings.title: Fully used federated recovery-code credential is never actually removed
findings.body:
`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now prefers the credential returned by the user storage provider. When all codes are used, the code still calls `removeStoredCredentialById`, which only touches the local Keycloak DB.

For a federated credential this does nothing. The id may even be null; for example, the test provider builds the model with `createFromValues` and never sets an id. The provider is never told to disable or replace its credential.

As a result, exhausted codes stay configured in user storage. `configuredFor` keeps returning true and the stale credential remains active. Removal for federated credentials should go through the provider, e.g. `disableCredentialType`, or be handled when new codes are created.

findings.title: Raw recovery codes sent to user storage and use is never tracked
findings.body:
The full list of plaintext recovery codes is serialized to JSON and passed as the challenge response to `updateCredential` of the user storage. Locally, codes are stored hashed and each one is consumed on use.

Nothing in this flow consumes a used code in federated storage. `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` built from the federated credential always reports the same next code, so the login bean always asks for code #1.

Unless every provider implements its own hashing and one-time consumption, recovery codes become reusable static secrets. The reference test provider in this PR does neither. This contract should be documented and enforced, or the codes hashed before they are handed over.

findings.title: getCredentials NPE when user not found; credential id missing
findings.body:
`getMyUser(user)` can return null, but `getCredentials` dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` without a null check. The other methods in this class all check for null.

In addition, the `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` built via `createFromValues` does not copy the stored id. The returned credential therefore has a null id, which breaks lookups and deletions by id.

findings.title: Test provider accepts any recovery code repeatedly
findings.body:
`isValid` returns true for any code in the list and never removes it. Codes can be reused indefinitely.

The new test therefore cannot detect that one-time semantics are lost for federated recovery codes. It only exercises the first code once.
